issue: The stem includes $150,000 spent 'designing the logo' and keys only the $12,000 of registration and legal fees as capitalized. Widely used texts treat design costs of an internally developed trademark as capitalizable, so distractor (b) '$162,000; not amortized' is defensible. The stem also never says the company intends to renew, which the key's explanation ('a renewable trademark the company intends to renew') relies on to call the trademark indefinite-lived.
evidence: Blind answer d, but noted (b) as defensible. 12,000 + 150,000 = 162,000 = option (b). Kieso, Intermediate Accounting (Ch. 12, trademarks and trade names), lists 'attorney fees, registration fees, design costs, consulting fees, and successful legal defense costs' as costs of a company-developed trademark. ASC 350-30-25-3 expenses costs of internally developing intangibles that have indeterminate lives, which supports the key. Secondary sources found by web search disagree on design costs (some say expense, some list them as capitalized). Choice c's rationale and the item explanation rely on intent to renew; the stem says only that the trademark 'can be renewed indefinitely at minimal cost'. ASC 350-30-35-3 bases useful life on the entity's expected use and its ability and intent to renew.
source: ASC 350-30-25-3; ASC 350-30-35-3 to 35-4; Kieso, Intermediate Accounting, ch. 12; web search 'internally developed trademark capitalize design costs' (fylehq.com, upcounsel.com, simplestudies.com results conflict)
fix: Replace the contested cost with one that is clearly expensed: 'It spent $150,000 on consumer focus groups and brand research and $400,000 advertising it.' Then (b) $162,000 stays a wrong-rule distractor without ambiguity. Add 'and intends to renew it' after 'minimal cost'.

issue: Three pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis' and difficulty 3, two levels above their real skill. Each asks for a single rule with no facts to work through: how acquired IPR&D is first recorded (19), how successful patent-defense costs are treated (24), and how organization costs are treated (29). Items in the same module that test the same facts are labeled remembering/1: far-int-14 (start-up costs) and far-int-13 (R&D). These labels inflate the module's analysis share, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: Stems: 19 'How is it initially accounted for?'; 24 'How is the cost treated?'; 29 'How is the cost treated?'. Each has one fact and no computation. far-int-14 asks the same thing as 29 ('How are they reported?') and is labeled remembering/1. Module tally as labeled (practice + exam): remembering 8, application 10, analysis 13 (42%). Re-labeled by this review: remembering 12, application 17, analysis 2 (6%). FAR target: R&U 5–15%, application 45–55%, analysis 35–45% (content/sections/far.yaml).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Set far-int-19, -24 and -29 to skill 'remembering', difficulty 1. If the module needs analysis items, write them, for example a schedule of mixed intangible costs from several documents to classify, amortize and roll forward.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are one level off on these items. Every item from far-int-18 to far-int-29 carries analysis/3, whatever its content. 18, 21, 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 and 28 are single-rule applications (application, difficulty 1–2). Their near-twins carry lower labels: 23 and 20 are the same patent computation (20 is application/2), and 22 and 08 test the same fact (08 is application/2). far-int-17 goes the other way: it asks when capitalization of software for sale begins, which is pure recall (remembering), but it is labeled application/2. far-x2-22 tests the same fact and is labeled remembering/1.
evidence: One-step computations: 23 = 100,000 ÷ 8; 27 = 500,000 ÷ 10; 28 = 50,000 ÷ 5; 21 = 600/1,200 × 1,000,000; 18 = max(0.4 × 300,000, 300,000 ÷ 3). 22, 25 and 26 select one stem amount (15,000; 60,000; 90,000). With the item-002 relabels, the module moves from 13 analysis items (42%) to 2 (6%), against the FAR target of 35–45%.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml
fix: Set 18, 21, 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 and 28 to application. Set difficulty to 2 for 18 and 21, and to 1 for 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 and 28. Set 17 to remembering/1. To rebalance the module toward the Blueprint mix, add genuine analysis items, for example reconciling an intangibles roll-forward or finding errors in an amortization schedule.

issue: The `optional` (off-Blueprint) flag is applied inconsistently to goodwill and business-combination content. Under REVIEW.md P2-2, far-int-09 and far-x2-11 are optional because they test goodwill. But these remain core: the goodwill computation (03), bargain purchase (06), the private-company goodwill alternative (16, 27), IPR&D acquired in a business combination (19), the goodwill-formula and business-combination flashcards (fc4, fc5), and the lesson's goodwill section, faded example and objective 3 ('Compute goodwill arising in an acquisition'). A learner on default settings is drilled on goodwill in one item and has it hidden in the next.
evidence: items.json: only far-int-09 and far-x2-11 have optional: true. review/reference/blueprint-notes.md, Area II.F: 'Intangible assets. Finite-lived only: goodwill, indefinite-lived intangibles and internally developed software are BAR.' Its list of topics moved to BAR includes 'Indefinite-lived intangible assets, including goodwill and goodwill impairment' and 'Business combinations'. far-standards.md §1c: business combinations BAR (`verified`); goodwill BAR per Becker (`conflict` with docs/BLUEPRINT_NOTES.md). docs/BLUEPRINT_NOTES.md itself says business combinations moved to BAR and are 'not built as FAR content'. Same pattern as merged finding F-0377 (segments).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints via review/reference/blueprint-notes.md and far-standards.md §1c; REVIEW.md P2-2
fix: Decide goodwill's placement once and apply it everywhere. If BAR (the reference sheets' reading): mark far-int-03, -06, -16, -19, -27, fc4 and fc5 optional, and label the lesson's 'Goodwill' section and faded example 'BAR — optional' (or move them to an optional sub-lesson). If the expert confirms goodwill is FAR: remove the optional flag from far-int-09 and far-x2-11 and restore far-x2-11 to far-mock-1.

issue: Internally developed software is taught and tested as core FAR, though the 2026 Blueprints place it in BAR. This covers the internal-use software stages, cloud-computing implementation costs (which follow the same ASC 350-40 stages) and software for sale (ASC 985-20). REVIEW.md P1-7 added the lesson section and removed the earlier 'tested in BAR' note. far-x2-22 (software for sale) sits on the FAR mock exam far-mock-2, so the mock scores a BAR topic. Purchased software, a finite-lived intangible, stays FAR.
evidence: far-standards.md §1c: 'Internally developed or internal-use software (ASU 2025-06): No (BAR)', status `verified` (Becker, JofA). blueprint-notes.md II.F: 'internally developed software are BAR'. A web search returns a BAR task-based guide titled 'BAR CPA exam: how to calculate capitalized software developed for internal use or for sale and the related amortization expense' (superfastcpa.com). content/far/exams/far-mock-2.json line 14 lists far-x2-22. None of 11, 12, 17, 18, 25, 26 or x2-22 is optional.
source: AICPA 2026 BAR Blueprint (via far-standards.md §1c; https://www.superfastcpa.com/bar-cpa-exam-how-to-calculate-capitalized-software-developed-for-internal-use-or-for-sale-and-the-related-amortization-expense); REVIEW.md P1-7
fix: Mark far-int-11, -12, -17, -18, -25, -26 and far-x2-22 optional. Replace far-x2-22 on far-mock-2 with an in-scope finite-lived intangible item that has the same key letter. In the lesson, keep the purchased-software paragraph as core and label the internal-use/cloud-computing part 'Tested in BAR — optional for FAR'. Record the reversal of P1-7 in REVIEW.md.

issue: Several items test rules the lesson never teaches. Software to be sold (ASC 985-20) is tested in four items: capitalize from technological feasibility to general release, and amortize at the greater of the revenue ratio and straight-line (17, 18, 25, x2-22, the last on far-mock-2). IPR&D acquired in a business combination is capitalized as indefinite-lived (19). Equipment with alternative future uses is capitalized, and its depreciation is R&D expense (28). No other FAR lesson covers these. The lesson can mislead: it says 'Software is different — purchased software and internal-use software development costs can be capitalized' and states flatly that 'Research and development costs are expensed (ASC 730)'. A learner who applies that to items 19 and 28 gets them wrong.
evidence: grep of content/far/modules/*/lesson.md for 'technological feasibility', '985-20', 'in-process', 'IPR&D' and 'alternative future use' finds no matches. Only the item explanations mention these rules. The 18 key (120,000 = max(400/1,000 × 300,000, 300,000 ÷ 3)) needs the greater-of rule, which is taught nowhere.
fix: If these items stay, even as optional, add a short 'Software to be sold' box to the lesson: expense to technological feasibility, capitalize to general release, amortize at the greater of the revenue ratio and straight-line, with a worked line. Also add an 'R&D exceptions' note: equipment and materials with alternative future uses are capitalized and depreciated, and acquired IPR&D in a business combination is an indefinite-lived intangible until completion or abandonment. Otherwise retire the items, or move them to an optional BAR module (see finding 005).

issue: Some core items test indefinite-lived intangible mechanics and R&D rules for their own sake, which the 2026 Blueprints place in BAR. far-int-07 tests reassessing a license from indefinite-lived to finite-lived and the impairment test that goes with it. far-int-13 is the bare ASC 730 rule. far-int-28 tests R&D equipment with alternative future uses. fc2 covers indefinite-lived impairment and reassessment. None is optional. By contrast, items that use these rules only to decide what is capitalized or amortized for finite-lived assets (01, 04, 08, 22) support the FAR tasks 'identify costs to capitalize' and 'calculate amortization' and can stay core.
evidence: blueprint-notes.md II.F: 'Finite-lived only: goodwill, indefinite-lived intangibles and internally developed software are BAR'. Its list of topics moved to BAR includes 'Research and development costs'. far-standards.md §1c: R&D costs BAR (`verified`).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints via review/reference/blueprint-notes.md and far-standards.md §1c
fix: Mark far-int-07, -13 and -28 optional, and fc2 optional (or reword fc2 to the FAR-relevant point: 'Indefinite-lived: not amortized'). Apply the same decision as finding 004, so the treatment matches.

issue: These items sit in far-intangibles, so a miss sends the learner back to this lesson, which does not teach what they test. The lesson says only 'Goodwill is not amortized by public companies; it's tested for impairment (see the impairment module).' The one-step goodwill impairment computation (x2-11), annual testing at the reporting-unit level (09) and the private-company 10-year amortization alternative (16, 27) are taught in far-impairment.
evidence: far-impairment/lesson.md lines 87–113 teach the reporting-unit test, the one-step loss capped at goodwill, and 'Private companies may elect to amortize goodwill (straight-line, generally over 10 years or less)'. far-intangibles/lesson.md has no mention of 'reporting unit', '10 years' or the private-company alternative.
fix: Change far-x2-11's moduleId to far-impairment. Add one sentence to this lesson's Goodwill section: 'Public entities test goodwill at least annually at the reporting-unit level; private companies and NFPs may elect to amortize it straight-line over 10 years or less and test only on a triggering event.' Alternatively, move far-int-16 and -27 to far-impairment.

issue: Flashcard fc6, 'Always expensed', lists 'research & development' as always expensed. That contradicts the module's own items: acquired IPR&D is capitalized (far-int-19), R&D equipment with alternative future uses is capitalized (far-int-28), and software development costs after technological feasibility are capitalized (far-int-25). The card also says 'always' and then lists 'most advertising', which contradicts itself. A five-term list is not atomic.
evidence: far-int-19 key: 'As an indefinite-lived intangible'. far-int-28 key: R&D expense of 10,000 on a 50,000 asset, i.e. capitalized. far-int-13 choice d explanation: 'expensed, except tangible assets with alternative future uses'. ASC 730-10-25-2(a) and (c).
fix: Retitle it 'Expensed as incurred (GAAP)' with back 'Start-up and organization costs; internally generated goodwill and brands; advertising (generally)'. Add a separate card: 'R&D: expensed as incurred, except equipment and materials with alternative future uses (capitalize, then depreciate or charge to R&D as used) and IPR&D acquired in a business combination (capitalize).'

issue: Four numeric distractors match no misconception from the stem facts, and their rationales name no error. 05(c) $20,000 'uses a 12-year life', but no 12-year figure appears in the stem. 18(c) $80,000, 23(d) $10,000 and 28(d) $25,000 are each explained only as 'Not the computation.' An informed test-taker can rule them out at once, so each item effectively has three options.
evidence: Python: 05c 240,000 ÷ 12 = 20,000 (the stem gives only a 10-year term and a July 1 date). 18c 80,000 only reproduces by contrived paths, such as 0.4 × (300,000 − 100,000), which is no known error. 23d 100,000 ÷ 10 = 10,000, but no 10-year figure is in the stem. 28d 50,000 ÷ 2 = 25,000, with no 2-year basis in the stem.
fix: Replace each with a modeled error. 05: add 'renewable for 10 more years at the franchisor's option' and use (c) $6,000 = 240,000 ÷ 20 × 6/12 (renewal assumed although not assured). 18: (c) $200,000 = 400 ÷ 600 × 300,000 (current ÷ remaining revenue instead of ÷ total). 23: (d) $100,000 (expensing the purchased patent like R&D). 28: (d) $40,000 (reports the carrying amount instead of the expense). Each rationale should name the error.

issue: Several distractor rationales either fail to name the error that produces the number or are circular, and several trap labels misfit. 20(c) $8,000 and 23(c) $5,000 come from dividing by the 20-year statutory patent term; the rationales say 'Use the useful life.' and 'Not the computation.', and the trap is distractor-number. far-int-chk1(c) names this error correctly. 25(c) $180,000 capitalizes every cost; its rationale is 'Not the computation.' and its trap distractor-number, where overgeneralization fits. 21(b) $400,000 assigns the residual after recording equipment at full fair value; its rationale is 'Use relative fair values.' and its trap distractor-number, where wrong-rule fits. 24(b) 'Not the treatment.', 24(d) 'That is not the rule.', 29(b) 'That is not permitted.' and 29(c) 'Not the treatment.' teach nothing.
fix: 20c and 23c: 'This divides by the 20-year statutory patent term; use the shorter of remaining legal life (15) and useful life (8).' Trap wrong-rule. 25c: 'This capitalizes all costs; pre-feasibility costs are R&D and post-release maintenance is expensed.' Trap overgeneralization. 21b: 'This records equipment at its full fair value and gives the patent the residual; allocate cost by relative fair value (600/1,200).' Trap wrong-rule. 24b: 'Legal defense costs are not prior-period items; they go to the asset or to expense.' 24d: 'There is no split; the outcome of the suit decides capitalize vs. expense.' 29b: 'GAAP gives organization costs no asset treatment.' 29c: 'Only stock issuance costs reduce equity; incorporation fees are expensed.'

issue: On these calculation items, the item-level explanation states the rule in one sentence and shows no computation. The key's choice explanation is often just as bare: 18's key says only 'The greater of revenue ratio (40%) and straight-line', with no amounts. Items 01–14 show the computation; 15 and 18–28 do not.
evidence: Example, 18: 'Amortization is the greater of the revenue-ratio amount or straight-line.' The needed working is 400/1,000 × 300,000 = 120,000 vs. 300,000 ÷ 3 = 100,000, so 120,000. Example, 15: 'Costs of successfully defending a patent are capitalized and amortized over the remaining life.' The needed working is 120,000 − 2 × 12,000 = 96,000; + 24,000 = 120,000; ÷ 8 = 15,000.

issue: Several items carry answer cues. 04: the key ('renew indefinitely') echoes the stem's 'indefinite-lived', and the key is the longest option. 16: the key is the only option with a hedge ('or less') and the longest, while distractor d is an absolute ('Never'). x2-22: all three distractors carry absolutes ('All costs', 'Only costs', 'No costs ... always expensed') and the key has none. chk2: the key is much the longest and the only option that mentions a purchase. 09: the key is a sentence fragment ('Not amortized; tested annually ...'), while a, b and d all read 'It is/It can be ...'.
evidence: cues.md flags 04 (key longest), 16 (key longest; absolute in d), x2-22 (absolutes in a, b, d), chk2 (key much longest). The 04 word echo and the 09 grammatical mismatch were checked by hand.
fix: 04: key 'A trade name that the company can renew every 10 years at minimal cost and intends to renew'. 16: make the key 'Amortized straight-line over a period not exceeding 10 years' and give d a hedge too ('Tested for impairment only at year-end'). x2-22: remove the absolutes (a 'Costs from product planning through general release'; d 'Costs after general release'). chk2: shorten the key ('A customer list purchased from a competitor') and lengthen one distractor. 09: write c as 'It is not amortized and is tested at least annually at the reporting-unit level.'

issue: These are two pairs of near-clones, while core finite-lived tasks go untested. 20 and 23 are the same item: a purchased patent with 15 years of legal life and an 8-year useful life, amortized as cost ÷ 8. far-int-chk1 and the lesson's worked example test the same thing. 10 and 15 are the same computation: (carrying amount + successful defense) ÷ remaining life, which far-int-24, fc3 and the lesson's worked example also cover. Untested: no item asks for an intangible's carrying amount at a balance-sheet date, a change in an intangible's estimated useful life, a purchased-software amortization, or the cloud-computing amortization and expense line. Objective 4 of the lesson and the FAR finite-lived carrying-amount task cover these.
evidence: 20: 160,000 ÷ 8 = 20,000. 23: 100,000 ÷ 8 = 12,500. Same structure (15 legal / 8 useful). 10: (120,000 + 30,000) ÷ 6. 15: (96,000 + 24,000) ÷ 8. A web search lists a FAR Area II practice set titled 'Calculating the Carrying Amount of Finite-Lived Intangible Assets' (superfastcpa.com).
source: Review standards §2, per-MCQ check 7; AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint Area II.F
fix: Rewrite 23 as a carrying-amount item: a patent bought April 1, Year 1 for $100,000 (8-year useful life); carrying amount at December 31, Year 2 = 100,000 − 100,000/8 × 21/12 = 78,125. Rewrite 15 as a change in estimate: after 2 of 10 years, the remaining useful life is revised to 4 years, so 96,000 ÷ 4 = 24,000. Add one purchased-software or cloud-computing amortization item.

issue: The stem omits the depreciation method, the salvage value and the date the equipment was placed in service. The key assumes straight-line, zero salvage and a full year of use.
evidence: Key 10,000 = 50,000 ÷ 5 (straight-line, no salvage, full year). Double-declining balance would give 20,000; a half-year convention would give 5,000.
fix: Reword: 'Equipment costing $50,000 (5-year life, no salvage, straight-line) that has alternative future uses was bought on January 1 and used in R&D all year.'

issue: The `calc` flag is set on items that need no arithmetic. Each key is one amount copied from the stem, with costs sorted into capitalize or expense. far-int-11, the same kind of item, is correctly calc: false.
evidence: 01 key 12,000 (stem amount); 22 key 15,000 (stem amount); 25 key 60,000 (stem amount); 26 key 90,000 (stem amount). far-int-11 key 80,000 (stem amount) has calc false.
source: Review standards §2, per-MCQ check 5 (calc only for items that need a computation)
fix: Set calc to false on far-int-01, -22, -25 and -26. Alternatively, add a second capitalizable cost to each, so the learner must add them.

issue: The internal-use software stage table puts 'data conversion' in the post-implementation/operation stage. Under ASC 350-40, data conversion usually happens during application development but is still expensed, as training is. A learner given 'data conversion during the application development stage' could wrongly capitalize it.
evidence: Lesson table row 3: 'Post-implementation / operation (training, maintenance, data conversion) | Expense'. ASC 350-40 requires data conversion costs (other than for software needed to convert data) to be expensed as incurred, even when they arise in application development, and ASC 350-40-55 describes them as typically incurred in that stage.
source: ASC 350-40-25 (data conversion and training costs); ASC 350-40-55
fix: Move data conversion out of the stage list. Add a line under the table: 'Training and data conversion are expensed whenever they occur, even during application development.'

issue: The lesson's citations list omits authorities the body relies on: ASC 350-40 (internal-use software and cloud-computing implementation costs; ASU 2018-15; ASU 2025-06), ASC 730 (R&D) and ASC 360-10 (impairment of finite-lived intangibles).
evidence: Frontmatter citations: 350-30, 350-20, 805-30-30-1, 720-15 only. The body cites ASC 730, ASC 360 and ASC 350-40 inline.
fix: Add 'FASB ASC 350-40 (Internal-use software; cloud computing arrangements)', 'FASB ASC 730-10 (Research and development)' and 'FASB ASC 360-10-35 (Impairment of long-lived assets)' to citations.
